description: Open-source cellular RF planning workspace for real-map propagation, interference analysis, and bounded network optimization.

summary.one_liner: A.T.O.M is an open-source, planning-grade cellular RF planning workspace that models 4G/5G (and an experimental 6G profile) coverage, interference, and bounded azimuth optimization on OpenStreetMap-based data for Ankara, Turkey.
summary.what_it_does: The app lets users place two to eight cells on a map of a dataset region (the bundled dataset is Ankara) and evaluate baseline coverage using deterministic RF estimation from OSM and OpenCellID-derived data. It produces received-power surfaces and colored diagnostic rays, plus 4G/5G interference metrics such as RSRP, SINR, RSRQ and RSSI. It runs bounded azimuth optimization scored on POI and residential demand, propagation reach and overlap, and includes per-cell explanations and feasible Pareto solutions. Additional tools cover a coverage gap finder, building-entry estimates, candidate cell recommendations from existing records, and validation of up to 5,000 RSRP samples. Results are exported as local Markdown/HTML reports and project/ZIP files, and the Dataset Pack Studio builds packs for other geographies. The README states these are planning estimates, not measured propagation accuracy.
use_cases: Compare azimuth options for a small urban cell plan
Visualize 4G/5G coverage and interference on a real map
Find underserved buildings within a sector beam
Evaluate candidate sites among existing cells in a search area
Validate model predictions against drive-test RSRP samples
Build and export reproducible RF planning reports for review
how_to_run: git clone the repository, cd atom, and run git lfs pull
Open the app in a browser and check readiness with curl
cd backend-go && go run ./cmd/validate-dataset ../data-pipeline (optional, validates bundled dataset pack)
notable: Deterministic ray tracing with bounded Go worker pools and an in-memory R-tree spatial index, with no database required
Explicit model-provenance labeling: urban LOS/NLOS path loss kept separate from legacy wall-event loss, and research profiles (6G 140 GHz, sub-THz, reflection) isolated from canonical RF
Map-first four-stage workflow (Plan, Simulate, Analyze, Review) with local autosaved projects, scenario versions and run history
Optional 5G Core Lab overlay showing Xn, N2 and N3 communication paths with a separate adapter sidecar
Dataset Pack Studio and validated dataset switching for arbitrary regions via schema-v2 packs
caveats: Results are planning estimates from static OSM and OpenCellID data; the README states measured real-world propagation accuracy is not yet established and they are not drive-test or PHY measurements
Sector engine does not model reflection-heavy multipath, fading, multiple-edge diffraction, or MIMO scheduling; interference is limited to 4G/5G and the 6G profile is experimental
The bundled Ankara building dataset is 111 MB via Git LFS, and heavier workloads depend on hardware; the README qualifies capacity only for a specific 2 CPU / 4 GiB profile
